input.evidence: The capacity check is in dogwhistle/allocation.py (A). It sets CAPACITY = 2 (line 12). feasible_assignments() (lines 16-19) keeps only assignments where every vendor's count is at most CAPACITY. validate_assignment() (lines 36-42) rejects anything that isn't a list of N_ITEMS valid vendor letters, then returns the indices only if they are in FEASIBLE, so over-capacity assignments are rejected there. I put A first because it holds the logic the request describes. The other files don't contain it. gate.py (B) has only public_refs, handoff, lexical_rejection and deliver, with no capacity or count logic. stats.py (D) has only sign_flip_one_sided, bootstrap_lower and summarize. listener.py (C) imports and calls validate_assignment but doesn't define the check. The required_memory_refs are A and C, so the private pair is B and D. They get 40 of the 60 minutes (20 each), mainly to confirm that they don't duplicate or bypass the capacity check. That leaves 15 minutes for A and 5 for C.
